output.name: Tesmar — The Lamp Boat
output.myth: When the sea took my cousin's boat off the Leeward rocks, we did what we always do. At the harbour mouth we said every name aloud, and for each we lit a lantern on Tesmar's rail. Tesmar is a boat of salt-wood and promises. She sails up into Vel one fist north-east of the Drying Shag, where the drowned stand on the skerries with their arms out to dry, then come aboard to mend nets in her hold. The Salt Pot hangs to the north, the pot the sky keeps: one pinch of every lamp goes into it, so nothing is lost from the count. Kael casts from her stern for fallen stars and has never hauled one in, which is why he is so cheerful. Sil comes down each month to count the lamps, because she still searches for Aun, and some nights she thinks he is in the hold. Orrun shifts beneath the hull and the sea goes quiet. Hesk will not say when the boat will come home. So keep saying the names. A lamp is light enough for anyone to carry.
output.finding: Find the Drying Shag low over the Leeward water, then go one fist (about 10°) north-east of it to reach Tesmar, the lamp-strung boat.
